blockers: Flow 3b — the H2 bar `/login`'s Set-Cookie carries `Max-Age=2592000` was never observed at runtime (`Set-Cookie header(s) = []`), because Playwright's APIRequestContext sends `Accept: */*` and `middleware.ts:134` only stamps the marker when Accept includes `text/html`. This is the one bar round 4 exists to prove and it is unverified. Cheap re-drive (server must be restarted; ~1 min): from apps/web start `npx next dev -p 3007`, then `curl -sS -D - -o NUL -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 16_5 like Mac OS X) AppleWebKit/605.1.15 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/16.5 Mobile/15E148 Safari/604.1' -H 'Accept: text/html' http://localhost:3007/login` and read the `set-cookie:` line — it must contain `rf-mobile-app=1` and `Max-Age=2592000`. Alternatively re-run the same request inside the spec with `headers: { accept: "text/html" }` on `ctx.request.get`. Until that header is seen, the H2 narrowing is proven only by source + `middleware.marketing.test.ts:219`, not by a served response.
judge.reasoning: branchBuildProven is TRUE and I confirmed it independently (dev-server.log paths + compiles under the worktree; the r4-wholesalers desktop shot shows the ported marketing header nav), so no flow is void for wrong-build reasons — the round-3 blocker is discharged. I then judged every bar from the pixels rather than from the driver's summary, and re-derived both contrast numbers with my own full-region samplers (apps/web/test-output/r4/judge-sample.mjs, judge-note.mjs, judge-crop2/3.mjs — all under the now-ignored test-output/, confirmed by `git check-ignore -v apps/web/test-output` -> .gitignore:46, `git status --porcelain | grep -c test-output` -> 0, so H1 also holds and my scratch files do not dirty the tree). Four bars pass. Flow 1: 13.88:1 against a 3:1 bar, white mark on the dark teal panel, visually confirmed at 3x. Flow 2 passes but the driver's evidence for it was OFF-TARGET — `getByText(\"Book a distributor demo\")` matched the navy CTA pill, so the driver measured button-fill vs page (14.9:1) and never touched the `.hero-note` the C1 ruling is about; I found the note one row-block below the pill and measured its core ink at rgb(107,118,135) = #6b7687 = 4.60:1 vs white at BOTH 1440 and 375, which clears the 4.5:1 bar with a 0.10 margin. Flow 3a passes cleanly: /brand and /signup come from Next with no rewrite, / is rewritten only when rf-mobile-app=1 is present and returns the 129908-char marketing HTML when it is not. Flow 4 passes on both DOM facts and my own reading of the three cropped hero viewports — one h1 each, word spaces intact, zero console errors, zero failed same-origin requests. Two flows are unverified and I refuse to round either up. Flow 3b: /login IS proxied, but no Set-Cookie was emitted for the request the driver made, so the Max-Age=2592000 half of a conjunctive bar has zero runtime evidence; source and the unit test corroborate but do not substitute for a served header, and this is precisely the H2 change round 4 was convened to prove — hence the single blocker, with the exact one-line curl to close it. Flow 5: /dashboard rendered as a bare spinner unauthenticated, the sidebar never mounted, so H3's two tone="light" call sites are unproven by pixels; the ruling pre-authorised marking this unverified, so it is not a blocker — but note the /login substitute cannot even attribute the white ink to H4's new CSS rule, since that element also carries the Tailwind brightness-0/invert pair. Net: land-blocking work is one ~1-minute re-drive of a single request; everything else the UI gate was asked to prove is proven.

verdicts.evidence: `git diff -- .gitignore` = one hunk, `+apps/web/test-output/` after `test-output.txt`. `git -C <worktree> check-ignore -v apps/web/test-output` → `.gitignore:46:apps/web/test-output/	apps/web/test-output`, exit 0. `git status --porcelain | grep -i 'test-output'` → no match (grep exit 1). Refuting W4a's framing: the 21 MB is out of git, but it is NOT out of the TypeScript program — see hazard N1; the regate's 4th item ('60+ untracked files') is a mis-applied check (the port is uncommitted, so every new port file is legitimately untracked; the ruling's actual criterion — test-output gone from the list — is met).

middleware.ts:68 `const MOBILE_APP_COOKIE_MAX_AGE = 60 * 60 * 24 * 30;` used at :139; docblock lines 60-65 say '30-day ROLLING marker'; middleware.marketing.test.ts:219 asserts /Max-Age=2592000/i. `grep -rn 31536000` over apps/web (excluding node_modules/.next/test-output) → no output, so nothing still pins the 1-year value. I did NOT take the executor's or the unit suite's word: I wrote, ran and deleted my own probe `app/(marketing)/zz-reviewer-probe.test.ts` against the real `middleware()` export — 7/7 PASS, and it closes the UI judge's blocker (flow 3b) at the code level with the Accept header the driver omitted. P1 /login + Accept: text/html → rewrite `https://routeflowmobile-production.up.railway.app/login` AND set-cookie printed verbatim: `rf-mobile-app=1; Path=/; Expires=Wed, 07 Oct 2026 12:59:42 GMT; Max-Age=2592000; HttpOnly; SameSite=lax`. P2 `/_expo/static/js/web/x.js` (Accept */*) → rewritten, marker null. P3 `/` + marker cookie → rewritten to `${MOBILE_WEB_URL}/` and RE-STAMPED with Max-Age=2592000 (the 'rolling' claim holds). P4 `/` with no marker → no rewrite, no marker (marketing home). P5 `/?desktop=1` with the marker, and `/login` with `prefer-desktop=1` + the marker → no rewrite, no marker (opt-out wins at any age). P6 `/brand/routeflow-mark-192.png` and `/signup` → no rewrite, no marker (served by Next). P7 the emitted Max-Age is exactly 60*60*24*30. Probe file deleted afterwards: `git status --porcelain | grep zz-reviewer` → no match. Residual, honest: this exercises the middleware function, not a served Next response; the only unexercised layer is Next's own dev plumbing, which the judge already proved for the rewrite half.

verdicts.item: H3 — TenantLogo tone prop + two sidebar call sites
verdicts.evidence: components/TenantLogo.tsx: `tone?: BrandTone` (default `"dark"` at :39) is forwarded ONLY to the no-logo fallback (`` at :55); the tenant-uploaded path (:49-53) is still a plain `` with no tone, no brand-mark class — so the hunted 'tone leaks into the tenant logo' hazard does NOT exist. `app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx` +`tone="light"` at :1313 (lg+ rail) and :1363 (mobile drawer), both on the bg-navy sidebar; the third caller (`app/(dashboard)/invoices/[id]/page.tsx:2318`, white/print surface) correctly keeps the default dark. Import is from `./brand/BrandMark` (the index barrel re-exports only values, not the `BrandTone` type) — W4a's transient TS2305 is GONE: `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` now reports zero errors in any round-4 file. `npx jest components/brand --runInBand` → 17/17 pass. Not pixel-proven (dashboard is client-gated; the UI ruling pre-authorised 'unverified'), and the /login substitute cannot attribute the white ink to H4's CSS because that element also carries `brightness-0 invert`.

Implemented exactly as ruled — globals.css:217 `.brand-mark--light { filter: brightness(0) invert(1); }`, and marketing.css:9705 `.rf-marketing .brand-mark:not(.brand-mark--light) { mix-blend-mode: multiply }` with object-fit/flex-shrink left on the bare selector at :9701 — BUT it turns the suite RED. `npx jest --silent` (apps/web) = Test Suites 1 failed/41 passed, Tests 1 failed/337 passed: `pinned global styles — MKT-PIN T7 › app/globals.css is byte-identical to the branch baseline` expected 09d7d3dc…, received e38149e6…. This is unambiguously round-4's doing: `git show HEAD:apps/web/app/globals.css | sha256sum` = 09d7d3dc… and `git show 5ddec78e:apps/web/app/globals.css | sha256sum` = 09d7d3dc… (identical), and `git diff --stat 5ddec78e -- apps/web/app/globals.css` = 1 file, 10 insertions — i.e. the ONLY delta from the pinned baseline is H4's block. The design of record and the port's own containment test contradict each other: T7 exists to prove the port does not touch globals.css. W4b's gate (`jest components/brand`) could not see this. Separately, the multiply scoping is inert today: `grep -rn 'tone="light"'` hits only login, dashboard×2, platform-admin, buyer login, buyer portal — no `app/(marketing)` surface renders a light mark — so it is defensive only, and no marketing mark on a light ground is broken by it (multiply against a near-white ground is a near-identity anyway).

Half fixed. Both edits landed (marketing.css:5110 `#5c6b82`, :5115 `#6b7687`) and they DO win the cascade — a brace-depth scan of marketing.css shows :1378/:1403 and :5107/:5112 are all top-level with equal specificity, so the later pair wins. But the WCAG computation used the wrong ground: the ruling and W4b both measured against white, while `.rf-marketing .connection-diagram` is repainted OPAQUE `#eeedf2` by a LATER unqualified rule at marketing.css:8636-8639 (also top-level, so it overrides the `#edf3fb8c` at :5091). I measured the shipped pixels rather than reasoning alone — pngjs scan of `apps/web/test-output/artifacts/r4-product-375x812.png` (the only page that renders the diagram: `app/(marketing)/product/page.tsx:93,100`): a contiguous `238,237,242` band at y 7291-7450; `#5c6b82` ink pixels at y 7366-7369 with modal surround `238,237,242`; `#6b7687` ink pixels at y 7320-7416 with modal surround `238,237,242` (107 of 125 neighbour samples). Contrast against that real ground: #5c6b82 → 4.65:1 (PASSES); #6b7687 → 3.95:1 (FAILS the 4.5:1 bar the ruling set). For reference the same colours on white are 5.41 and 4.60, and the originals were 2.95 / 2.73. So `.rf-marketing .connection-diagram > p` is still sub-AA where it actually renders; it needs a tone with relative luminance ≤ 0.150 on #eeedf2 (e.g. #5c6b82 itself, already proven at 4.65:1), or the ground re-ruled.

newHazards.summary: H1 ignored apps/web/test-output/ in git but not in the TS program: tsconfig `include` is `**/*.ts`, `exclude` only `node_modules`, so the pipeline's scratch spec keeps `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` at exit 2 (3× TS7006 in test-output/r3/r3.spec.ts) — the gate cannot go green. The judge's own r4 scratch (test-output/r4/judge-*.mjs) now lives there too, so this recurs every round. Durable fix: add "test-output" to `exclude` (one line, owned by nobody in round 4); deleting the r3 scratch only defers it.

Ruling H4 as written cannot be satisfied without breaking the port's own containment pin: marketing-port.static.test.ts:309/356 (MKT-PIN T7) asserts globals.css is byte-identical to branch base 5ddec78e, and globals.css at HEAD still matches that hash exactly. Needs a lead re-ruling — either re-pin GLOBALS_CSS_SHA256 with the reason recorded next to it (T7's stated purpose is 'the port must not touch globals.css', so a silent re-pin weakens the guard), or move `.brand-mark--light` out of globals.css (marketing.css is scoped to .rf-marketing and cannot cover the login/buyer/platform-admin shells, so a small unscoped brand.css imported by the root layout is the likelier home), or drop the belt-and-braces rule since BrandMark already emits `brightness-0 invert`.

H5's contrast maths assumed a white ground for elements that sit on `.rf-marketing .connection-diagram`'s opaque #eeedf2 (set later, unqualified, at :8637). Measured on the shipped r4-product screenshot, `.connection-diagram > p` #6b7687 = 3.95:1 — still below AA. Any future contrast ruling on this stylesheet must name the EFFECTIVE ground (a 10k-line concatenation where a later unqualified rule silently repaints the container), not the page background.

The H3 swap replaced the fallback `` with ``, which renders `alt="" aria-hidden="true"` — so the no-logo fallback lost its accessible name, and the component's `alt` prop is now silently ignored on that branch (still honoured on the tenant-logo branch). Net a11y is acceptable today because all three call sites pass `showName` (the business name renders as adjacent text, and the mark is genuinely decorative), but the dead `alt`/`fallback` props are a trap for the next caller: `fallback?: "seller" | "buyer"` is still declared in the interface while the implementation no longer reads it, so a future `fallback="buyer"` would be silently dropped.

`.brand-mark--light` is unlayered plain CSS at line 217, after `@tailwind utilities` (line 3), so on a tie of specificity it WINS over Tailwind's filter utilities on the same element. Harmless today (identical effect to the `brightness-0 invert` pair BrandMark also emits), but it means any future filter utility on a light mark — `drop-shadow-*`, `grayscale`, `blur-*` — would be silently discarded, and the two mechanisms can drift apart unnoticed. If the rule survives the H4 re-ruling, prefer one mechanism (the class) over belt-and-braces, or scope it inside `@layer utilities`.

review.reasoning: Refute-first, everything re-derived rather than taken from the executor summaries. Two of the five rulings do not land as claimed, and both are cheap to close. H1 and H2 hold. H2 I re-probed with my own throwaway spec (written, run at 7/7 PASS, deleted — `git status` clean of it), which also discharges the UI judge's single blocker: the judge saw `Set-Cookie: []` only because Playwright's APIRequestContext sends `Accept: */*` and middleware.ts:134 gates the stamp on `text/html`; with the header supplied, `/login` is proxied AND emits `rf-mobile-app=1; Path=/; …; Max-Age=2592000; HttpOnly; SameSite=lax`. Every other contract point the lead asked me to re-probe passes: no marker on a non-HTML rewrite, `/` proxied and re-stamped with the marker, `/` marketing without it, `?desktop=1` and `prefer-desktop` winning at any age, `/brand` and `/signup` served by Next. H3 holds and the specific hazard I was told to hunt — a tone leaking into the tenant-uploaded logo path — does not exist: the `logoUrl` branch is an untouched plain ``. H4 is implemented exactly as designed and still turns the suite red: `npx jest --silent` is 337/338 with the one failure being MKT-PIN T7, the pin that exists to prove the port never touches globals.css. HEAD's globals.css hashes identical to the pinned baseline, so this is round 4's own doing and not inherited. That is a design-vs-test collision the ruling did not reconcile, so it needs a lead decision (re-pin with a recorded reason, relocate the rule, or drop it), not an executor improvisation. H5 is the finding I would have missed by reading the diff. The two colours land and win the cascade, and both numbers are right — against white. But the element they colour sits on `.connection-diagram`, which a LATER unqualified rule at marketing.css:8637 repaints opaque #eeedf2. I measured the shipped r4 product screenshot rather than arguing from the cascade: the `#6b7687` ink pixels are surrounded by `238,237,242`, giving 3.95:1 — still sub-AA. The nodes' `#5c6b82` survives at 4.65:1. Half the ruling therefore did not achieve what it was for. Gates: tsc is still exit 2, but purely from a scratch spec under the now-git-ignored test-output — H1 removed it from git without removing it from the TS program, and the judge's own r4 scratch now lives there too, so this recurs every round until `test-output` is in tsconfig's `exclude`. Lint is green (0 errors) and the regate's untracked-files item is a mis-applied check against an uncommitted port. Prettier is clean on all six files (`--check` → "All matched files use Prettier code style!"). Net: three concrete blockers — the T7 pin, the tsc exclude, and the `.connection-diagram > p` tone — none of which is more than a few lines, but the first needs a lead ruling because the design of record and the port's own guard disagree. One more round.
